messages:
From: ops@aurora-inc.com

Cc: sre@neptune.ai
Date: 2027-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusually high latency and errors this morning — we need a plan

Olga / Redwood team,

We saw a sharp spike in end-to-end latency across us-west and us-east starting ~08:45 PT and a correlated increase in 500 errors for our batch-processing endpoints. Impacting ~18% of traffic and delaying downstream jobs. Our engineering and SRE teams are blocked on a couple of questions: do you have any indication this was a capacity or routing issue versus a model-serving regression? We need a timeline and a mitigation plan — our execs are asking for an interim workaround and customer communication.

Attachments: aurora-incident-timeline.csv

— Aaron Li
Director of Platform Operations, Aurora Systems

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: ops@aurora-inc.com, sre@neptune.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusually high latency and errors this morning — we need a plan

Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the timeline. We're triaging now. Quick status:
- Initial telemetry shows elevated tail latency and increased token recompute rates on a subset of hosts.
- Early hypothesis: combined effect of a rollout of a new kernel selection policy + an uneven autoscaler reaction to a traffic burst.
- Immediate mitigations in progress: pin affected customers to last-stable model variant, roll back kernel policy on the impacted pool, and scale up warm capacity in us-west.

I'll follow with an internal postmortem draft and a numbered action plan for the next 72 hours. Grace — please join the sync at 10:15 to coordinate the customer message and credits. Vivek — can you prioritize an indepth log export (kv-cache traces + kernel metrics)?

Attachments: s:

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ops@aurora-inc.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusually high latency and errors this morning — we need a plan

Thanks, Olga. I've drafted a short customer note for Aurora (below). Can we get confirmation on the rollback window and expected impact to their throughput before I send?

Draft note: 
Hi Aaron — we investigated and have applied a targeted rollback and temporary routing change to stabilize latency. You may see brief reconnects over the next 10–15 minutes as we drain affected capacity; overall throughput should return to normal within the hour. We will follow up with a technical summary and any credits for impacted consumption. — Grace, Redwood Ops

Lauren — please confirm the credit guidance we agreed (up to 20% for the time window 08:45–09:30 PT) and if procurement needs a formal note.

— Grace

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: sre@neptune.ai
Date: 2027-09-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusually high latency and errors this morning — we need a plan

Update from infra: we extracted kernel selection traces and KV cache churn logs. Early findings:
- A heuristic in the new kernel selector mis-classified short-context, high-conc currency requests and picked a slower path for ~23% of requests.
- The autoscaler reacted to elevated token compute by provisioning new hosts, but the new hosts were put into a different routing pool with incompatible routing policy, causing partial hotspots.
- Result: transient amplification of tail latency and 500s as requests hit suboptimal kernels and cold caches.

Short-term actions executed:
1) rollback kernel-selector change (deployed at 10:03 PT)
2) routing policy override placed to route Aurora to stable pool (10:10 PT)
3) warm pool capacity increased by +15% (10:18 PT)

I'll attach the raw traces to the shared drive and start a deeper causal analysis. Recommendation: emergency hotfix to kernel selector and a routing policy guardrail to prevent pool misassignment.

Attachments: https://drive.company/aurora/incident/20270912/rca-draft

— Vivek

- A proposed owner and timeline for the kernel-selector hotfix and the routing guardrail.
- Confirmation on credits and the wording we can share in their customer comms.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Head of Customer Success, ClearSky (supporting Aurora)

Thanks, Maria — closing the loop with the plan and owners. Deliverables (summary for exec readout + post-incident artifacts):
1) Exec readout (2027-09-14 09:00 PT): slides + quick timeline (owner: Olga) — DONE (attached draft).
2) RCA: root cause = kernel selector heuristic + routing-pool assignment bug; causal chain, mitigations already applied (rollback + routing override) and short-term stabilizers (owner: Vivek; ETA: 2027-09-16).
3) Hotfix & guardrail: production hotfix for kernel selector and a routing-policy guardrail to block pool misassignment (owner: Vivek; ETA: 2027-09-21).
4) Quality validation: extended canary for kernel-selector changes, synthetic load tests for cross-region bursts, and KV-cache health metrics added to SLOs (owner: Lauren; ETA: 2027-09-30).
5) Customer remediation & credits: up to 20% credit for the impact window, plus a one-week elevated support window (owner: Grace; formal note to procurement by 2027-09-15).
6) Follow-through tracking: weekly closure sprint updates in the Aurora channel and a final closure note when all items complete (owner: Olga; weekly cadence).
